basics.name: Kairong Luo
basics.summary: Third-year Ph.D. student at Tsinghua University working on scaling of language models, efficient training, open-source pretraining, and pretraining dynamics.

education.area: Third-year Ph.D. student in Department of Computer Science and Technology
B.S. in Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences (IIIS)

publications.name: Puro-2B: Poor Lab's Qwen2-1.5B Trained on RTX 5090 within $5090
publications.summary: An open, cost-efficient recipe for pretraining 2B language models on consumer-grade RTX 5090 GPUs, with the full data, code, and model weights released under Apache 2.0.

publications.name: RoBSA: RoPE-based Blockwise Sparse Multi-head Latent Attention
publications.summary: My contributions were experiment analysis and assistance with paper writing.

publications.name: How Learning Rate Decay Wastes Your Best Data in Curriculum-Based LLM Pretraining
publications.summary: Studies the mismatch between ascending-quality curricula and standard learning-rate decay in LLM pretraining, and shows that moderate LR decay plus model averaging recovers the gains of curriculum ordering.

publications.name: PCMind-2.1-Kaiyuan-2B Technical Report
publications.summary: Presents a fully open 2B language model and releases the complete stack around it, including model weights, dataset, preprocessing framework, and training framework. Its derived submission, Quantile Benchmarking Heterogeneous Web Corpora in Open LLM Pretraining, was selected as a NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight (Top 1.3%).

publications.name: Larger Datasets Can Be Repeated More: A Theoretical Analysis of Multi-Epoch Scaling in Linear Regression
publications.summary: Theory and LLM experiments show how dataset size affects useful data reuse. My contribution was to the experimental part of the paper.

publications.name: A Multi-Power Law for Loss Curve Prediction Across Learning Rate Schedules
publications.summary: Introduces a multi-power law that predicts loss curves across learning-rate schedules and helps identify better schedules than widely used defaults such as cosine decay.

publications.name: DreamFuser: Value-guided Diffusion Policy for Offline Reinforcement Learning
publications.summary: A trajectory-based value optimization approach that combines diffusion policy learning with efficient Q-function learning for offline reinforcement learning.
